mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES keeps edging up from its current depressed level, weekday commuting and lunch-trip traffic will spill into retail corridors and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise versus the previous 28 days even though WORKPLACES increases for at least two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in TRANSIT after a prolonged lull is a leading indicator of return-to-city shopping trips; if TRANSIT moves above its recent weekly average, RETAIL_REC will rise within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above its prior 3-week average after being below -34 for at least two weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above the stated threshold but RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the following 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while PARKS stays weak, people substitute toward neighborhood shopping and leisure retail rather than long-displacement outings, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 10 and PARKS staying below -20 for most of the period.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in PARKS mobility relative to the prior month diverts discretionary time away from retail and recreation, causing RETAIL_REC to soften over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while PARKS also rises above its current four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM turns negative after being near zero, households are likely reallocating trips into essential-only movement, which suppresses discretionary retail visits and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0 after staying at or above 0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 7 to 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM crosses below zero from a nonnegative run.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates a renewed mobility clampdown; retail and recreation then weakens with a short lag as destination trips are cut back.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 14 days after both proxies post two consecutive weekly declines.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains above its recent baseline and TRANSIT keeps lagging, more activity is being absorbed locally rather than through city-center trips, so retail demand stays subdued and RETAIL_REC falls over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 and TRANSIT remains below -30.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, gradual improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES restores access to commercial areas, and that combined accessibility shock lifts RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 28 days despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES trending upward from their current levels.
